# Hosts TypeScript SDK

TypeScript SDK for the Hosts API. Items kept in two regions.

The `Hosts` client is generated by flowapi from the API's description: 10 methods in 2 resources, each listed in [api.md](api.md) with its parameters and what it returns.

## Install

```sh
npm install hosts-sdk
```

## Usage

```ts
import { Hosts } from 'hosts-sdk'

const client = new Hosts()

const result = await client.items.all()
console.log(result)
```

A method takes its operation's parameters in one object, grouped by where each goes (`path`, `query`, `header`, `cookie`), with a body as `body: { contentType, value }`; it gives the response's body, read as the description says. A second argument changes one call (`headers`, `query`, `timeout`, `maxRetries`, `signal`). `withResponse()` gives the body with the raw response and the server's request id, `asResponse()` the raw response alone.

```ts
const { data, response, requestId } = await client.items.all().withResponse()
console.log(response.status, requestId, data)
```

The package is built twice, as ES modules and as CommonJS, each with its types, and depends on nothing: it calls the platform's `fetch`. From CommonJS the client is taken by its name, `const { Hosts } = require('hosts-sdk')`; `import Hosts from 'hosts-sdk'` gives it too.

## Resources

| Resource | Methods |

## Servers

The servers' URLs have variables. The client sends each one's default unless `serverVariables` gives another value:

| Variable | Default | Values |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `region` | `eu` | `eu`, `us` |
| `version` | `v1` | any |
| `zone` | `a` | `a`, `b` |

```ts
const other = new Hosts({ serverVariables: { region: 'us' } })
```

A value that is not one of a variable's values throws a `RangeError`.

A server URL may be relative to where the description is served (`./local`): give that address as `descriptionURL` to call it.

```ts
const near = new Hosts({ descriptionURL: 'https://api.example.com/openapi.json' })
```

## Errors

A response whose status is not a success throws an `APIError` with its `status`, `headers`, `body` and `requestId`, of the class for its status (any other status is an `APIError` itself):

| Status | Class |
| --- | --- |
| 400 | `BadRequestError` |
| 401 | `AuthenticationError` |
| 403 | `PermissionDeniedError` |
| 404 | `NotFoundError` |
| 408 | `RequestTimeoutError` |
| 409 | `ConflictError` |
| 422 | `UnprocessableEntityError` |
| 429 | `RateLimitError` |
| 500 and above | `InternalServerError` |

A request that gets no answer throws `APIConnectionError`: `APIConnectionTimeoutError` when an attempt took longer than its `timeout`, `APIUserAbortError` when its `signal` aborted it. These, and every other error the client throws itself, are `SdkError`s. A parameter the description does not allow throws `FlowapiRequestError` before anything is sent.

```ts
import { APIError } from 'hosts-sdk'

try {
  await client.items.all()
} catch (error) {
  if (error instanceof APIError) console.log(error.status, error.body)
  else throw error
}
```

## Retries and timeouts

A request that cannot connect, or is answered 408, 409, 429 or 5xx, is retried once by default when sending it twice does what sending it once does: its method is GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, TRACE, PUT or DELETE. A call of any other method (POST, PATCH) sends a random `Idempotency-Key` header, the same on each of its attempts, so that the server applies it once: it is retried like the others. The server's `x-should-retry` header decides first, where it sends one; a 403 is never retried. A retry that failed is not tried again: more retries are the caller's choice. Before each retry the client waits as long as the server asks in `retry-after-ms` or `Retry-After`, else 0.5 s doubled for each retry made, at most 8 s; when the server asks for more than 60 s, the error is thrown at once. Each attempt may take 60 s, its body read.

`maxRetries`, `timeout` and `maxRetryDelay` change these for the client, the last two in milliseconds; `maxRetries` and `timeout` change them for one call, in its options:

```ts
const patient = new Hosts({ maxRetries: 5, timeout: 120_000 })
await client.items.all({}, { maxRetries: 0, timeout: 5_000 })
```

## Logging

The client logs to `console` at `warn` and above. Set `HOSTS_LOG` to `off`, `error`, `warn`, `info` or `debug`, or give `logLevel`: at `info` it writes a line for each attempt, at `debug` the request's URL and headers too, with every credential written as `***`. `logger` sends the lines elsewhere.

```ts
const verbose = new Hosts({ logLevel: 'debug', logger: console })
```

## Requests no method makes

`client.request(method, path, options)` sends a request no operation of the description has, with the client's base URL, credentials, retries and errors; `asResponse()` gives the raw `Response`:

```ts
const response = await client.request('GET', '/').asResponse()
console.log(response.status)
```

## Requirements

Node 20 or later (CI runs 20, 22 and 24), or another runtime with `fetch`. Built with TypeScript 7.0.2.
